title: Two Beds, Ten Weeks
standfirst: Everything between today and first frost, ordered by how soon it stops being possible. The top block is the part with a closing window.

map.caption: The nine growing areas, drawn from your sketch and turned so north is at the top. Fill shows how much sun each one gets: the more gold, the more sun. Unfilled areas are the ones not yet surveyed.

beds.name: Street Bed 1
beds.aspect: Past the sidewalk, open to the north
beds.description: The cut-flower box. Dahlias, gaillardia, scabiosa, cosmos and sunflowers, all still going. Needs constant deadheading for the next ten weeks.

beds.name: Street Bed 2
beds.aspect: Past the sidewalk, open to the north
beds.description: Mostly finished and holding a lot of seed. One good clearing pass now, then it becomes the place hardy annuals get sown in September.

beds.name: Side Bed
beds.description: Narrow raised bed on the west wall. Strawberries, beans on string trellis, sunflowers and the compost tumbler. Shaded until midday, then hot afternoon sun off the wall, and sheltered from rain. That combination is what mildewed the sunflowers.

beds.name: Front Bed
beds.description: The shadiest ground you have. The house sits directly to its south, so it is in shadow for most of the day, and almost all day from October to March. Whatever is planted here needs to be a shade plant, and sun-lovers will always disappoint.

beds.name: Back Bed 2
beds.description: The best growing spot on the property and probably the most underused. A south-facing wall collects sun all day and radiates stored heat at night, which extends the season at both ends. It will also be the driest bed, in the wall's rain shadow.

beds.name: Back Bed 1
beds.aspect: South end, east of the driveway
beds.description: Detached from the house at the south end, past the driveway. Open on the map, so likely good sun, but nothing seen yet.

beds.name: Street Bed 3
beds.description: East side of the property beyond the driveway. Likely morning sun with afternoon shade, but that depends entirely on what stands to the west of it.

beds.name: Street Bed 4
beds.description: Same east strip as Street Bed 3, further south. Same open question about afternoon shade.

beds.name: Bed Path
beds.description: Rosemary, sage and a big stand of shasta daisy, with bearded iris through the middle and a bare patch at the front. The herbs thriving here is the evidence for full sun and sharp drainage. This bed wants the opposite of a fall tidy: the woody herbs must not be cut back until spring.

footnote: Ticking a box here is a local convenience for working at the bed. The durable record is content/plan.json. Frost timing is a ten-year average for in-city Seattle and varies by several weeks year to year, so treat November as a watch-the-forecast month rather than a dated one.
